trials.output_text:
A seed is like a tiny sleeping baby plant wrapped in a hard shell. It has everything it needs inside to start growing, but it needs the right conditions to wake up. When a seed gets water, warmth, and sometimes light, it begins to soften and swell. This tells the plant inside that it’s time to grow.

First, the seed sends a root down into the soil to drink water and get nutrients. Then a tiny shoot pushes up toward the sunlight. The shoot grows into a stem, and leaves begin to open. Leaves are like little solar panels that catch sunlight and help the plant make its own food.

As the plant keeps growing, it gets taller and stronger. It may grow flowers, and those flowers can make new seeds. Those seeds can fall to the ground and start the whole process again. That’s how a tiny seed can become a big plant, and how plants keep making more plants!
